section_path: 8.5 The Quantity of the Medicine Needed

note:
Paper 72, Team 34317. Fifty-four measured regions over thirty-one of the forty-seven pages, and all fifty-four are accounted for: thirty-five exhibit regions - twenty-three figures, seven numbered tables and five captionless grids - and nineteen exclusions, so unaccounted is zero and nothing is left unresolved. The paper numbers twenty-three figures and seven tables and every one of the thirty is here.

The paper's own habit is what makes this census unusual. It paints a white filled rectangle behind every line of type, and the measurer read those rectangles as illustrated blocks, so seven of the fifty-four regions are ordinary paragraphs and two integral display equations. The white fills separate them from real exhibits without a judgement call: every prose band carries 1.05 to 2.00 filled rectangles per text line and every pasted bitmap and drawn grid carries none. The same page-painting habit splits each flow chart into a chart region plus six fragments, because the node boxes are raster blocks dropped into a vector drawing, so the twelve fragment regions are excluded rather than counted as twelve more exhibits.

What the exhibits are. Twelve line plots carry the fitting and the sensitivity work, four are schematics - the two compartment graphs and the two flow charts - four are prefecture or county choropleths of the three countries, one is a dendrogram, one a clustered bar chart and one a three-dimensional exploded pie, and twelve are grids. The line plots come in two manufactures: the section 4 fit panels are pasted Matlab bitmaps, while the section 11 sensitivity charts are spreadsheet output with gridlines and category axes, and the change is visible in the type.

Eleven exhibit regions run wider than the paper's own 415.4 pt measure, led by Figure 4.9 at 116.7 per cent and Figure 4.8 at 114.8; Table 4.2 at 111.2 per cent puts a grid 46 pt into the right margin. Three of the four country maps overrun as well, by 3 to 12 per cent, because the bitmap inside them was pasted wider than the block; the Liberian map is the only one that fits.

Defects worth recording, in rough order of how much they cost a reader. Both compartment graphs end in a dangling arrow: Figure 4.1's F and Figure 4.5's F both point into empty white space with no target node, and Figure 4.5 redraws the same circle-and-arrow grammar without repairing it. On the delivery maps the word 'location' is drawn on top of the route polylines and the magenta A to F letters float 30 to 40 pt from whatever they label with no leader line, so the candidate sites have to be inferred; the legend bins are also non-monotonic on the three maps where the legend was read, from Guinea and Liberia, running 1-5, 6-30, 21-100, 101-500, 501-4000 - which makes two of the five classes of confirmed cases overlap. Figure 4.3, Figure 4.8 and Figure 4.9 all lost their right plot spine before pasting, so their right-hand y ticks hang detached inside the frames. Figure 4.3's left prediction curve is clipped by its own 3500 ceiling. Figure 4.7 prints no vertical-axis title at all. Figure 11.1 plots a parameter sweep on a date category axis, and Figure 11.2 draws a sweep of a few per cent on a zero-based bar scale where every bar is within a line width of its neighbours, so the chart cannot show the effect it was made to show. Figure 5.1 is a dendrogram, not the map the section and the caption both imply, and its caption collides with the leaf labels. Figure 4.2's fourth box reads 'GENETIC' alone, the operator noun dropped, and the subscripted f in its decision node overhangs the diamond.

Type and numbering. Every caption on the paper is printed in lower case with no space after the word - 'figure4.6:', 'table4.4:' - except on four pages where a space does appear (figures 4.1, 4.6, 4.7 and 8.2), so the caption layer is inconsistent with itself across the twenty-five pages that carry a caption. Sections 11.1 and 11.2 are used twice, once for the sensitivity work on pp41-42 and again for Strengths and Weaknesses and Overall Results on pp43-44, and the heading pass dropped the Roman-numbered 'IX Other Factors We Think Are Important' on p38 and '8.3 symbols and definitions' on p35, so Figure 9.1, Figure 9.2 and the p35 symbol grid hang off sections the index does not hold. Figure 11.2 is printed under the 11.1 heading although its caption and the 11.2 heading below it both describe the production-speed model, and that mismatch is recorded where the paper put it rather than corrected.

The five grids the paper prints without a name are the paper's quietest failure. Three of them are the route-length tables, each introduced only by 'the distances of them show in the table:', one of them holding six values under letters A to F for a sentence that itself drops route F; the p31 table is 349 pt wide and the other two are 109 pt, so the same content arrives at three different sizes with no unit and no number on any of them. The other two are symbol lists, one under 6.2 and one under 8.3, printed as ruled grids with no caption at all.

Citation practice is thin even by this lane's standards. Twenty-four of the thirty numbered exhibits are never named in the prose. The six that are - Figure 4.1 twice, Figure 4.3, Figure 4.6, Figure 4.7 twice, Figure 4.8 and Figure 8.1 - are every one of them cited on their own page, several of them in the sentence that follows the caption, so this paper never points backwards across a page break and never forecasts an exhibit to come.
rules: Panels are measured boxes, not figure numbers, so a two-panel exhibit drawn inside one measured region carries a panel_count of two rather than two rows [geometry.panel_count].

Full width means 75 per cent or more of this paper's own 415.4 pt text measure, never of the 595.32 pt page: Table 4.2 at 111.2 per cent is full and overruns the block, while every centred chart at 51 to 80 per cent is measured against the same number [table.width].

The paper splits its captions by exhibit type: all seven numbered tables print theirs above the grid and all twenty-three figures print theirs below the art, without one exception in either direction, which is why position is recorded per row rather than assumed - and the five grids that print no caption at all keep the default while caption_source stays none [caption.position].

This paper prints every caption in lower case with no space after the word - 'figure4.6:' on most pages, 'figure 4.6:' on a few - and the numbering vocabulary has no lower-case form, so num is recorded as 'Figure N:' and the printing is described in the note [caption.numbering].

A table with no number is still a table when it is a ruled grid inside the prose: the three 'distances of them show in the table:' grids carry an empty caption and a numbering of none by default, not a made-up number [caption.verbatim].

Seven of the fifty-four measured regions are ordinary prose, because this PDF paints a white filled rectangle behind every text line and the measurer grouped the rectangles into bands. The white fills give them away - 1.05 to 2.00 per line in the bands against 0.00 in every exhibit - which is why a region's area buys it nothing here [place.area_frac].

Two flow charts are each measured as one whole region plus six node fragments, because the nodes are raster blocks dropped into a vector drawing; the fragments are excluded as fragments of the chart rather than counted as six more exhibits, so the second region on p12 and the second region on p29 carry the whole drawing between them [place.page_order].
Where the prose cites an exhibit more than once, count records the printed instances outside that exhibit's own caption, and first_page the earliest of them [mention.count].

Section paths follow the printed heading above the block, so figure 11.2 is filed under 11.1 and figure 11.3 under 11.2, which is where the paper put them, not where their captions belong [place.section_path].

Two section labels are headings the heading pass missed - the Roman-numbered 'IX Other Factors We Think Are Important' on p38 and '8.3 symbols and definitions' on p35 - and both are accepted because each is a printed line of the text layer [place.section_path].

Twenty-four of the thirty numbered exhibits are never named in the prose at all; the six that are carry a count, and every one of those six is cited on its own page, so no exhibit on this paper is ever back-referenced across a page break [mention.lead_pages].

Note sentences are quoted from the layer that introduces the grid, which is why three of the six carry the paper's own errors - 'There are some symbols appear', 'We calculate all parameters in Guinea are' and 'parameters Sierra Leone:' [table.note_sentence].

caption.verbatim: table4.1: symbols in the model

tables.note: The model's symbol list, 410.6 by 462.0 pt at 98.8 per cent of the measure and the tallest grid on the paper: nine body rows under a SYMBOL, DEFINITION, UNITS head on a solid black band with knockout white capitals. Boxed - full outer frame, a rule between every row, no vertical between the columns. The symbol column is set in math italic and holds the paper's whole Greek inventory with subscripts and stacked fractions (beta_1, beta_2/beta_1, beta_F/beta_1, alpha^-1, gamma_1^-1, gamma_2^-1, gamma_F^-1, delta_1 delta_2, delta_2). Column widths are the defect: the DEFINITION column takes about 60 per cent of the grid, the SYMBOL column about 13 per cent - more than the short glyphs need - and UNITS about 27 per cent, so the middle column carries text wrapped to two lines in most rows while the other two stay half empty. Only two cells are tight enough to note: delta_1 delta_2 runs its two deltas together, and gamma_F^-1 crowds its raised -1 against the subscript.

table.note_sentence: There are some symbols appear in the model. We show them below:

caption.verbatim: table4.2: additional parameters and meanings in this advanced model

tables.caption_verbatim: table4.2: additional parameters and meanings in this advanced model
tables.note: The advanced model's hospital parameters: eight body rows under a SYMBOL, DEFINITION, UNITS header, 461.7 by 392.6 pt at 111.2 per cent of the measure, so the grid runs 46 pt past the text block. Fully boxed with a solid black header band carrying white capitals, a thin rule under every one of the eight body rows and the two outer verticals, but no interior column dividers and no zebra. Six of the eight definitions wrap to two centred lines, which is what makes the grid so tall. The symbol column is set in math italic and is the worst-set type on the paper: the raised -1 on h1, h2, gamma3 and gamma4 floats detached and above its subscript so the cell reads 'h1 ~1'; both gammas are drawn in an italic that reads as a lowercase y; and the two deltas in 'delta_1H delta_2H' run together with their H subscripts and no space.

caption.verbatim: table4.3: all parameters in Guinea

tables.note: The Guinea parameter set, 368.1 by 296.4 pt at 88.6 per cent of the measure, laid out as two SYMBOL/VALUE pairs side by side under a four-head band. Boxed, not booktabs: one outer hairline, a solid black header band with knockout white heads reading PARAMETER, VALUE, PARAMETER, VALUE, and no interior rule at all, horizontal or vertical - the eight rows are separated by white space alone, which is what the paper does on every one of its parameter grids. Cells are clean, nothing clipped.

table.note_sentence: We calculate all parameters in Guinea are:

caption.verbatim: table4.4: parameters of Liberia

tables.note: The Liberia parameter set, 377.0 by 295.1 pt at 90.8 per cent of the measure, the same two-pair layout as Table 4.3 and the same solid black header band with knockout white heads. Eight body rows, four columns, no interior rules, no cell merged, both value columns printed to two decimals throughout.

caption.verbatim: table4.5: parameters Sierra Leone:

tables.note: The Sierra Leone parameter set, 377.0 by 295.1 pt at 90.8 per cent of the measure, identical in construction to Tables 4.3 and 4.4: boxed outer hairline, black header band, eight body rows in two symbol/value pairs, no interior rule. The caption carries the paper's own stray colon - 'table4.5: parameters Sierra Leone:' - and is kept verbatim.

caption.verbatim: table5.1: differences between two supplies[3]

tables.note: A three-column comparison of normal against emergency supplies, 416.4 by 227.1 pt at 100.2 per cent of the measure, with ASPECTS, NORMAL SUPPLIES and EMERGENCY SUPPLIES across the top and six body rows - Aims, Formation, Property, Scheme, Balance Between Efficiency And Optimization, Delivery Mode. Rules run horizontally only, one under the header and one under each body row, with no vertical anywhere and no outer frame, so the grid reads as a stack of rules rather than a boxed table. The cells hold prose rather than data - 'Maximize Profile And Consider Both Fair And Efficiency' against 'Minimize Cost', 'Permanent' against 'Temporary', 'Return And Tour Return' - and each wraps to three or four lines, which is what makes six rows fill a third of a page. Cited only as 'the table below', never by number.

table.note_sentence: differences between them are shown as the table below:

tables.note: A small untitled SYMBOL/DEFINITION grid, 399.8 by 159.7 pt at 96.2 per cent of the measure, sitting directly under the 6.2 Symbols and Definitions heading with no caption and no number: the routing chapter's five symbols - c_ij, j, i, x_ij and H_1 - under a black header band and white small caps, a rule between the rows, no vertical between the two columns. Unlike Table 4.1 and Table 4.2 this list is Latin italic rather than Greek: the chapter it belongs to counts things rather than rates them. Not excluded, because it is a real ruled grid inside the text flow; recorded as a table with an empty caption and a numbering of none because the paper gives it neither.

The Guinea route lengths, a six-column one-row grid, 349.0 by 52.0 pt, no caption and no number: A through F across a black header band and 752.2, 686.6, 578.0, 546.5, 640.4 and 701.2 beneath them, in kilometres by inference only, since the grid carries no unit. This is the table the prose introduces as 'the distances of them show in the table:' immediately after the map, and the introducing sentence itself drops a route - 'A, B, C, D, E and represent the two route' - so the six values are matched to the six letters by eye. Clipped closed and clean otherwise.

caption.verbatim: table7.1: the six routes

tables.note: The six tours, 426.7 by 297.0 pt at 102.7 per cent of the measure: a narrow letter column A to F behind one internal vertical rule, and a wide column holding each tour as a chain of prefecture names in capitals joined by solid right-pointing arrowheads, from DUBREKA round six prefectures and back. Boxed - closed outer frame, a full-width rule at every one of the six row boundaries, and that one vertical for the letter column; no interior horizontals inside a row because a row is a chain, not cells. Rows A and E are the only two that wrap, and each continuation line begins with a bare arrowhead ('->COYAH->DUBREKA', '->KEROUANE->MACENTA') with no place name in front of it, so the wrap reads as a dangling lead arrow rather than a continued chain. The caption sits under the standfirst 'The route is listed:' and above the grid.

The Liberian route lengths, 109.0 by 52.0 pt, two columns and one body row: A and B on a black header band with 869.0 and 715.6 under them, the numbers the prose then turns into 'Therefore, the deliver location is Grand Bassa.' No caption, no number, no unit. At a quarter of the measure it reads as a floating fragment between two paragraphs, and the same construction appears again on the next page for Sierra Leone.

A one-row two-column distance grid, 109.0 by 52.0 pt, no caption and no number: A and B across the head and 411.4 and 616.9 beneath them, the two route lengths the prose introduces as 'the distances of them show in the table:'. Printed as a bare ruled box in the middle of a sentence, which is why the measurer caught it as a region at all. The last of the three such grids on the paper and, with the p33 r2 grid built to exactly the same 109 by 52 pt, one of the two smallest exhibits in the census.

The medicine-production chapter's symbol list, 356.1 by 303.5 pt at 85.7 per cent of the measure, boxed, eight rows under a SYMBOL/DEFINITION head on a black band. It has no caption of any kind - not above it in the fourteen points before the grid and not below it - and is introduced only by the section heading '8.3 symbols and definitions', which is the one heading on the paper printed in lower case after its number. The symbols run from V_1 through lambda_i^-1, so this is the fastest-production-rate chapter's notation: the exhibit that says what the medicine-speed model's terms mean, printed without a name.
